answer: To resist Sybil attacks, require every agent to lock a slashable bond before earning reputation; if evidence proves coordinated fraud, validators burn that agent’s bond. An attacker creating N identities must immobilize N bonds for the unbonding period, so attack cost rises linearly with N and detected fakes lose their stake. A cipher commitment links each identity to its history, while glacier-length withdrawal delays rapid reuse; a lagoon of independent validators checks the evidence.
